newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Victoria to open up energy retailing.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Victoria to open up energy retailing.

text.p: Australia's Victoria state on Wednesday signalled it would throw open competition for retail electricity consumers, announcing gas, water and other utilities would be allowed to sell power into the home.
Victoria Treasurer Alan Stockdale said the state government wanted to ensure strong competition for households, which would be able to shop around among electricity retailers from 2001.
"I think over time the distinction between the utilities will be blurred," Stockdale told reporters.
Initially power utilities will enter the retail market for telecommunications, but in the long term telecoms are likely to do the reverse and start selling electricity to homes, he said.
"In the long run, there's no reason why telecoms and companies involved in the water industry, (and) the transport companies, could not get into the utilities industries generally," he added.
The Victoria government's three state-owned gas retailers, due to be privatised by the end of 1998, are looking at selling electricity into the home from 2001, Stockdale said.
